To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the SMA has detected four submillimeter sources behind the massive clusters A370 and A3390.

the SMA resolves two of our sources, A2390–3a and A370–2, and measures their fluxes, while the flux of A2390–1 is consistent with the SCUBA flux and its redshift is 1.8, and that the SMA does not detect A2390-2.

we have resolved A370-2 into two components, that we have resolved the A2390-2 into two distinct submm sources, that the A2390 sources have redshifts between z = 1.8 and z = 4.7 and that the submm counts have a faint end slope of -1.1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the properties of SMGs, which are believed to be the progenitors of massive elliptical galaxies at z > 2.
the study of high redshift galaxies and their evolution.
the detection and study of high-redshift galaxies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the faint-end 1.2 mm counts are still uncertain by a factor of 2.5.
the submillimeter counts are still not well constrained at the faint end.
our new results are consistent with previous results, but with more accurate measurements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the submillimeter number counts are not as steep as previously thought, which implies that there are more submillimeter sources at fluxes below the SCUBA limit than previously thought.
our observations confirm the existence of a population of SMGs at high redshift and that the number counts are consistent with a steep power-law distribution.
we have detected two of the four lensed SCUBA sources with the SMA and have resolved A2390- 3 into two components.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gravitational lensing is a powerful tool for studying the faint end of 850 μm source counts.
the faint end of 850 μm number counts is likely to be steeper than previous estimates.
the submillimeter flux densities of the lensed SMGs are significantly lower than predicted by the power-law fit to the faint-end counts.
